unit.can_do_en: ask about a form and say what I need.

brief.situation_en: Maria calls the bank. Tiina answers.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Hi! My bank card has gone missing.

lines.speaker: Tiina
lines.text_puhe: Voi ei. Mä suljen sen heti. Mikä sun nimi on?
lines.text_kirja: Voi ei. Minä suljen sen heti. Mikä sinun nimesi on?
lines.gloss_en: Oh no. I'll block it right away. What's your name?

lines.speaker: Tiina
lines.gloss_en: OK, the card is now blocked.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Good. Can I get a new card?

lines.speaker: Tiina
lines.text_puhe: Joo. Se tulee postis viikon päästä.
lines.text_kirja: Kyllä. Se tulee postissa viikon päästä.
lines.gloss_en: Yes. It comes in the post in a week.

lines.speaker: Tiina
lines.gloss_en: No, a new card is free.

forms.form_name_en: nominative singular, with the possessive ending for my

forms.why_en: This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
'What.' A question word in nominative singular, asking what the price is.

forms.form_name_en: nominative singular, with the possessive ending for your

forms.why_en: Means 'is': present tense, 3rd person singular, going with 'Helsinki'.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Means 'now'. Leo asks where home is at this time.
Means 'good!' or 'great!', showing you are happy.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 1st person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö

forms.why_en: Yes. In everyday speech people often say joo instead.
'It.' Nominative singular, referring back to the price.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.

forms.form_name_en: partitive singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö

forms.why_en: Means 'new', describing Maria herself: 'I am new here'. Spoken: 'uus'.
